title: DECAF Score
aliases: Dyspnea Eosinopenia Consolidation Acidemia atrial Fibrillation score
sources: Steer J, Gibson J, Bourke SC. The DECAF Score: predicting hospital mortality in exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. Thorax. 2012;67(11):970-976.
DECAF versus CURB-65 to Foresee Mortality among Patients Presenting with an Acute Exacerbation of COPD (validation literature).

changelog.change: Initial entry — a genuine content gap (Content audit 2026-09-14, Batch 3). All 5 components and risk bands WebSearch-verified against the 2012 Thorax derivation paper, including the extended-MRC-Dyspnea 5a/5b split.

purpose: In-hospital mortality risk for an acute COPD exacerbation, at the point of admission — helps identify who's safe for early supported discharge (low risk) versus who needs closer monitoring or escalation planning (high risk).

items.label: Extended MRC Dyspnea (eMRCD) scale
items.help: Grades 1-4 = able to leave the house unaided. 5a = too breathless to leave the house, but independent with washing/dressing. 5b = too breathless to leave the house AND needs help washing/dressing.

items.label: Atrial fibrillation (known history, or new on this presentation)

interpretation.label: Low risk (0-1)
interpretation.detail: Low in-hospital mortality risk — a candidate for early supported discharge pathways where available.

interpretation.label: Intermediate risk (2)
interpretation.detail: Individualize disposition; not clearly low or high risk on this score alone.

interpretation.label: High risk (3-6)
interpretation.detail: Substantially elevated in-hospital mortality — favor admission with close monitoring and early escalation planning (NIV readiness, ceiling-of-care discussion).

buildNote: The eosinopenia cutoff (< 0.05 ×10⁹/L) is the opposite direction from the eosinophil-guided-steroid literature elsewhere in respiratory medicine (where LOW eosinophils predict a poor steroid response) — both point the same clinical direction here (low eosinophils = sicker, more likely bacterial-driven exacerbation), but flagged in case a future editor assumes it's a copy-paste error from a steroid-responsiveness module. Companion to bronchiolitis-management/croup-management as the third major respiratory-exacerbation scoring tool, though for a different age group and disease.
